big_idea: Same AMOUNT, different COINS. 50¢ has many combinations.
learning_intention: We are learning to make 50¢ in 3 different ways.
student_learning_goal: I can make 50¢ in 3 different ways.
success_criteria: I can MAKE 50¢ with mixed coins.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Tappy the Frog — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.

minds_on.hook: Tappy the Frog: Friends — same AMOUNT, different COINS! 50¢ has THREE ways! Tappy opens: 'SAME AMOUNT — MANY WAYS! TAP TO PAY!' (Class echoes.)
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Tappy the Toonie Frog puppet (green felt with toonie pendant). 'Money friends — last year we named coins. This year we make EQUIVALENT amounts!'

Define EQUIVALENT. 'EQUIVALENT = SAME VALUE, different coins. 50¢ can be MANY ways.'

Demo 3 ways for 50¢:
- WAY 1: 2 QUARTERS (25¢ + 25¢ = 50¢).
- WAY 2: 5 DIMES (10+10+10+10+10 = 50¢).
- WAY 3: 1 QUARTER + 2 DIMES + 1 NICKEL (25+10+10+5 = 50¢).

Place each combo on the chart visibly. Class checks each total.

'Tappy says — same TOTAL. Different COMBINATION!'

Demo a 4th way. '10 NICKELS = 50¢ also!' Stack them up.

Now show what's NOT equivalent. '4 quarters = $1, NOT 50¢. Don't mix amounts!'

'Tappy says — count the VALUE, not just the COINS!'

Now each pair gets Coin Cards + a Record Strip. Target: 50¢. They find 3 ways.

'Tappy says — pick ANY combination. Just total 50¢!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Coin Cards + Record Strip. Pairs find 3 ways to make 50¢.
Record each combo on the strip.
Stretch: find a way using a 50¢ coin alone.

INVENT-AND-COMPARE: After Tappy demos ONE way, pairs invent their OWN combinations FIRST, then class compares: 'Whose combo uses the FEWEST coins? Whose uses the MOST? All 50¢?' Cite Sowder (1992) flexibility-of-representation.
steps.teacher_prompt: Tappy: 'Same TOTAL, different COINS. Math is about the AMOUNT, not the pieces.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to coin stations and stack. NO-MATERIALS PATH: children show 50¢ with fingers — each open hand = 25¢ (a quarter), each finger held up = 10¢ (dime), thumb = 5¢ (nickel). Body becomes the wallet.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: makes; verifies total; records; finds 3; explains.

discussion_prompts: Tappy's preview: tomorrow Loonie Lou shows us 100¢ = TWO 50¢ stacks (Lesson 2 — F1.1). Hold onto your dimes!
consolidation.exit_routine: Tappy + Lou refrain — Tappy calls 'SAME AMOUNT —' Class: 'MANY WAYS!' Tappy: 'TAP TO PAY!' (3x). Each child writes 3 ways to make 50¢ on a sticky.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 1 sets the baseline for equivalence.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child mixes coin counts but the TOTAL is wrong — repairing the wrong-total trap at Grade 2
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On 'show 50¢ multiple ways', the dominant Grade-2 trap is fixed-combination thinking — child knows 2 quarters = 50¢ but cannot generate alternatives. Sowder (1992, 'Estimation and Number Sense') and Carpenter & Moser CGI work on part-whole composition place flexibility-of-representation as the gateway to fluent money work. Without it, Lessons 2-5 cannot ground.

Today: invent multiple 50¢ combos. Tomorrow Loonie Lou shows 100¢ = TWO 50¢ stacks (Lesson 2 — F1.1). Lesson 3 bills + coins; Lesson 4 hundreds; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Combo activity. Child writes '4 quarters + 1 nickel = 50¢'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Tappy asks — let's count. 4 quarters = ___?'

Probe. '25 + 25 + 25 + 25 = $1. + nickel = $1.05. NOT 50¢!'

Generalise. 'Tappy says — count the VALUE. Each quarter = 25¢. 4 quarters = $1. We need 50¢, so 2 quarters!'

If still confused: skip-count. '25, 50, 75, 100 = $1.'
common_misconceptions: More coins = more amount. (Repair: count value.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child names coin values but adds wrong: scaffold skip-counting by 25s, 10s, 5s; child counts up TO 50 with matching coin sounds.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can't name a coin's value: drop back to Lesson 1 of g1 unit pattern (name → value → combine).
DIAGNOSTIC C — child finds ONE combo and stops: ask 'show me a DIFFERENT way to make 50¢' explicitly; demand at least 3 alternatives before progressing.

parts_outline.task: Show 3 ways to make 50¢ with coin pictures.
For 3 mixed combos, mark TRUE if total = 50¢.
Make 50¢ using ONLY dimes — how many?
